THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD  DATED 10.07.2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.2801/2012 ON THE FILE  SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT  CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BAILHONGAL, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF  COMPENSATION.
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:805  MFA No. 101278 of 2016  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though the matter is listed for admission, with the consent of the parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. Appeal by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation in respect of road traffic accidental death of one Gadigeppa Gangappa Talawar that occurred on 24.10.2012 at about 6.45 a.m. involving tractor and trailer bearing Nos.KA-49/T-4732, No.KA-49-T-5203 and No.KA- 49/T-3943.

The tribunal on consideration of the material evidence on record including the objections raised on behalf of the insurance company of the Tractor and trailer unit, allowed the claim petition by awarding a compensation in a sum of Rs.6,41,980/-.
3. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation, claimants are in appeal.

Sri.Hanumanth R.Lathur, learned counsel for the claimants reiterated the grounds urged in appeal memo contended that the tribunal has not assessed the quantum of compensation properly inasmuch as monthly income is notionally assessed in a sum of Rs.5,000/- and it should have been assessed at Rs.6,500/- p.m. and sought for enhancement of compensation.
5. He also contended that tribunal has not granted compensation under the head filial affection and sought for allowing the appeal.

6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri.M.Y.Katagi, opposed the appeal grounds and contended that tribunal has wrongly taken the deduction of the income at  when there are two claimants and it should have been at 1/3 and therefore, sought for dismissal of the appeal.
7.

Having heard the parties and perused the material available on record, this court is satisfied that claimants have made out a case for reassessment of compensation NC: 2024:KHC-D:805 inasmuch Smt. Fakkirawwa vs Shri. Dhareppa on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169477443/
2 as on the ground of taking notional income, tribunal has erred in assessing the monthly income in a sum of Rs.5,000/- p.m. as against sum of Rs.6,500/- p.m.
So also, on the other heads, tribunal has not granted the compensation properly.

8. Hence, quantum of compensation is reassessed under difference heads as under:
Sl.No. Name of heads Amount(Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 6,29,200-00 (7150X12X2/3X11) 2
Towards consortium 80,000-00 3 Funeral and Estate 30,000-00 4
Medical expenses 52,796-00 Total 7,91,996-00 9.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed.
ii) As against compensation of Rs.6,41,980/-
claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,91,996/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:805 iii) Four weeks time is granted for insurance company to deposit the balance compensation.
iv) Claimants are not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 564 days in filing the appeal.
v) Ordered accordingly.

Sd/-
